RAJYA  SABHA

List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the August 27, 2007/Bhadrapada 5, 1929 (Saka)

(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource

Total number of questions — 20

Achievement levels of KV students
*201. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Kendriya Vidyalaya
Sangathan has conducted any survey of the
achievement levels of its students in English,
Maths, Science and SST for classes VII
and VIII;
(b) if so, the results thereof and the steps
taken to further augment the achievement
levels;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether Kendriya Vidyalaya, INA
Colony has taken up any such quality
assessment of its students for class VIII;
(e) if so, the results thereof; and
(f) if not, by when the Kendriya
Vidyalaya Sangathan intends to initiate it?
 Power to all by 2012
*202. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to provide power to all by
2012;
(b) if so, what is the estimate of total
power requirement of each State and UT in
2012, the sources of supply and their
capacities to provide power;
(c) what directions have been given to
State Electricity Boards and power
distributing agencies to ensure that
transmission lines are ready in time to
supply power available for consumers; and
(d) the authority designated to co-
ordinate for ensuring planned construction
and commencement of production,
distribution of power to distributing
agencies and transmission to consumers?
 Gas required by the power sector
*203. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI VIRENDRA BHATIA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) the quantum of gas being made
available to the power sector from the
exploration of D6 block of KG basin;

64
(b) the approximate requirement of gas
for the power sector; and
(c) whether the Ministry had taken up
the matter with the concerned Ministries
for allocation of natural gas for
implementing its projects and if so, the
outcome thereof?
 Minority educational institutions
*204. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether many States have minority
educational institutions;
(b) if so, the number of educational
institutions including schools, colleges,
professional colleges and self-financing
professional colleges of various categories
that had applied and have been granted
minority status during the last three years,
year-wise, category-wise and State-wise;
(c) the total number of students and the
students of various minority communities
enrolled in above educational institutions
during that period, year-wise, category-
wise, State-wise and institution-wise;and
(d) the number of the above educational
institutions run by minority communities
during that period, category-wise,
community-wise, State-wise and
year-wise?
 Indo-US power agreement
*205. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether any agreement in the power
sector has been signed during his recent
U.S. visit;
(b) if so, to what extent the agreement
is likely to help in improving the sagging
power situation in the country;
(c) whether any power plants by the
American companies are proposed to be
set up in the country, as per the agreement;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise?
 Status of houses under Bhakra
Management Board
*206. SHRI TARLOCHAN SINGH:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of Government houses in
the Nangal township which are now under
the control of the Bhakra Management
Board, category-wise;
(b) the number of occupied houses and
those lying vacant and the period for which
they have been vacant;
(c) the condition of these houses; and
(d) whether there is any policy to save
these houses and, since Government
Officials demand is not there, whether these
could be given on rent to private persons?
 Question patterns in written tests
*207. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether NCERT has suggested re-
vamping the question patterns in written
tests, with more emphasis on short-
answer-type and multiple-choice
questions;
(b) whether NCERT has discussed the
matter with the Education Boards in the
country;
(c) the names of the Boards with which
NCERT has held discussions; and
(d) the reaction of each of the Boards
regarding the matter?

65
 Improving the conditions of
homebased women workers
*208. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) what action Government propose
to take in the wake of Hon'ble Prime
Minister's remarks made in April, 2007 that
perhaps there is, in our societies, a cultural
bias for women to be in homebased work;
(b) if so, whether its further
compounding, through increase in sub-
contracting and outsourcing, resulting in
higher percentage of homebased women
workers to 51 per cent in 2005 from only
35 per cent in 2000 would be controlled;
and
(c) what measures are on the anvil to
ensure that skills and variegated experiences
of women workers are utilized in nation
building activities at par with those of male
workers?
 New panel on mineral policy
*209. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up a
new panel on mineral policy to attract
investors;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what were the short-comings as per
the Hoda Committee report; and
(d) how far it is proposed to address
those issues?
 Setting up of solar energy plants
†*210. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of NEW
AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of solar energy plants
being set up in the States, as on date;
(b) the total amount spent thereon, so
far;
(c) by when each of these plants are
likely to be commissioned;
(d) whether Government propose to set
up such plants, particularly in rural areas
during the current financial year; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
 Persistent drop-out of students
*211. SHRIMA TI  VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of  HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether  it is a fact that the children
in the age group of 6-12 years are getting
dropped out from schools persistently in
the country;
(b) if so, whether Government have
formulated any concrete policy to enhance
the enrolment of such children in schools
to reduce the drop-out rate; and
(c) if so, the salient features of the
policy?
 Electrification of Rajasthan villages
through solar and bio-gas energy
*212. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of NEW AND
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of villages electrified
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

66
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
through solar and bio-gas energy in
Rajasthan during the last three years;
(b) whether Government have launched
any scheme/programme to provide energy
derived from sun and bio-gas to rural areas
of the State;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
promote NCES in the country, particularly
in remote rural villages?
 Outreach programmes of NIOH
*213. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the National Institute for
the Orthopaedically Handicapped (NIOH),
Kolkata has stopped its outreach
programmes;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether NIOH has received
demands to help people in Andhra Pradesh;
(d) when the Institute conducted an out-
reach programme  last in that State;
(e) whether follow-up camps would be
held by the Institute; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
 Reduction of ST seats in Jharkhand
Legislative Assembly
†*214. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
any proposal of the Delimitation
Commission to reduce the number of seats
reserved for Scheduled Tribes in Jharkhand
Legislative Assembly;
(b) if so, the information available with
Government in this regard; and
(c) Government's policy in this regard?
 Committee to review NCTE
*215. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have set up a
committee to review the performance of
the National Council for Teachers'
Education (NCTE);
(b) if so, the details of the major findings
and recommendations of that committee;
and
(c) the action taken on the findings and
recommendations thereof?
 Reservation for Backward Classes
and Dalit Muslims
†*216. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is fact that Justice
Rangnath Mishra Commission has
recommended for reservation in Government
services and educational institutions for
Backward Classes and Dalit Muslims;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether her Ministry has
recommended not to implement the same;
and
(d) if so, the facts in this regard and the

67
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
decision taken by Government in this
matter?
 High schools under Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan
*217. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that high schools
would be brought under the Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the status of primary schools under
SSA in Assam;
(d) the number of schools brought under
SSA purview in that State;
(e) whether any discrepancies have been
reported under the SSA;
(f) if so, the steps taken to eliminate the
same; and
(g) the number of primary schools
serving Mid-Day Meals in Assam?
 Education for masses
*218. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether students with 90 per cent
marks find no place in the admission list of
various colleges, higher educational
institutes and top professional courses;
(b) whether this is due to educational
opportunities having not grown in line with
economy and even the private sector
has failed so far to make a dent in this
area; and
(c) if so, the action Government propose
to take to provide education for masses
and reduce the rising cut offs in colleges, as
besides professionals, the country also
needs middle level workers with median
salaries and all kinds of qualifications, who
are doing well in the rising economy?
 Working of NIOH, Kolkata
*219. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of SOCIAL
JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
allow the National Institute for the
Orthopaedically Handicapped (NIOH),
Kolkata to develop as a multi-campus
institution;
(b) whether there is any demand at
present to replicate the outreach programme
of the institute directly in remote areas of
the country;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the funds allocated for this purpose
for 2007-08; and
(e) the measures proposed to expand
such outreach activities?
 Survey by NUEPA
†*220. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the report of survey conducted by National

68
University of Educational Planning and
Administration (NUEPA);
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
are not serious regarding the target of total
literacy;
(d) if not, who is responsible for the
said situation; and
(e) the action Government propose to
take in this regard?

 Generation of tidal energy
1519. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of EARTH
SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to generate
tidal energy in the country;
(b) whether Government have
formulated any scheme for generating
affordable energy from sea waves; and
(c) if so, the details thereof, indicating
the status of the project?
 Workers in food processing industries
†1520. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the approximate number of workers
working in the food processing industries
in the country, at present;
(b) the number of those, out of the
above, who are working in the unorganised
sector; and
(c) what has been the overall growth
rate of this industry during the current year?
 Upgradation of Cochin University
1521. PROF. P. J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to upgrade the Cochin University of Science
and Technology into an institute of national
importance;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the action taken in this regard; and
(d) the benefits that would accrue
including the financial assistance, by
upgrading the status of the University?
 Books on sex education
†1522. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government

351
intend to effect some changes in the books
on sex education prescribed in the schools
throughout the country with the help of
UNESCO/UNO;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) if not, the details thereof; and
(d) the objectives behind imposing sex
education on the students despite strong
opposition to it throughout the country?
 Schools with pucca buildings in
Jharkhand
1523. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of primary, middle and
secondary schools in Jharkhand that do not
have pucca buildings;
(b) the number of schools that have a
teacher for each class and how many
schools have teachers who have to teach in
more than one classes;
(c) the figures of such schools with the
teacher teaching classes 2, 3, 4 and 5 all
alone and by when the teacher and the
classroom ratio would be reduced to 1:1;
and
(d) in what manner Government
propose to improve the situation?
 Increasing seats in higher education
1524. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to increase
the seats in higher technical institutions like
Indian Institutes of Technology, Indian
Institutes of Management, etc.;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
 Financial outlay for higher and
technical education
1525. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Education Committee on
Financing of Higher and Technical
Education has recommended that 6 per cent
of GDP should be set aside for education,
of which one per cent should be earmarked
for higher education and 0.5 per cent for
technical education;
(b) whether the Working Group has also
suggested that the total financial outlay for
this sector during the Eleventh Five Year
Plan should be Rs. 39,402.50 crore,
compared to the Tenth Five Year Plan
allocation of Rs. 4,700 crore;
(c) if so, whether Government have
agreed to these suggestions; and
(d) by when a final decision, in this
regard is likely to be taken?
 Absence of head of institutions
1526. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian
Institute of Advanced Studies, Mussouri,
the Indian Institute of Management,
Lucknow, The Indian Institute of
Management, Kolkata, the National School
of Drama and the Council for Scientific and
Industrial Research are without the head of
institutions;
(b) if so, for how long these institutions
have been running without heads;

352
(c) whether there are any other major
institutions without the top managerial
personnel; and
(d) the reasons and constraints in
appointing the heads of the institutions
promptly without delay?
 Applications for setting up of foreign
universities
1527. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
a number of applications for establishment
of foreign universities;
(b) the stand of the University Grants
Commission on establishment of such
universities in the country;
(c) whether a separate body would be
set up to oversee these foreign universities;
and
(d) the steps proposed to help students
who have studied in institutions which
have collaborated with foreign universities?
 Funding pattern of SSA
1528. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to change the funding pattern of
the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) whether it is a fact that some States
had protested this funding pattern?
 Central University in every State
1529. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the manner in which the Prime
Minister's endeavour to have a Central
University in every State and a degree
college in every district is proposed to be
fulfilled by his Ministry;
(b) whether this is a major thrust area
of his Ministry in the Eleventh Five Year
Plan;
(c) whether it is a fact that the Planning
Commission and the UGC has been asked
to prepare a strategy in this regard; and
(d) the extent to which the above vision
of the Prime Minister would help in
improving the Gross Enrolment Ratio in
higher education in the country?
 Universities recognised by UGC
1530. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of universities recognized
by the University Grants Commission;
(b) whether there is a proposal by the
Commission to classify universities on the
basis of their academic standing and other
criteria;
(c) if so, the guidelines developed to fix
a status or a category;
(d) whether any professional
accreditation body has been identified to
do the assessment; and
(e) the details of steps proposed to
upgrade the standards of education and
discipline in all the universities?
 Revenue collected through education
cess
†1531. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the amount of revenue collected by
Government through education cess;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

353
(b) on which educational programmes
the amount of education cess is spent;
(c) whether the States with the literacy
less than national average are provided
special assistance from this amount; and
(d) the amount allocated to Madhya
Pradesh Government from this amount
during 2005, 2006 and 2007?
 Setting up of IISER in Andhra
Pradesh
1532. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up an Indian Institute of Science Education
and Research (IISER) at Tirupati in Andhra
Pradesh;
(b) whether Government have received
any proposal from the State Government;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the reasons for delay in setting up
of the above institute; and
(e) by when the above institute is likely
to be set up?
 Educational schemes for Punjab
1533. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of cases for grant
submitted by Punjab Government for
various education schemes relating to higher
education, pending with the University
Grants Commission as on 31st March,
2007, under various heads; and
(b) since when each such case has been
pending and the time likely to be taken to
decide them?
 Sanctioning of D. Ed. colleges
1534. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Maharashtra Government
has informed the NCTE not to sanction
any more D. Ed. college in State;
(b) whether Government have also given
directives to NCTE not to sanction new
D. Ed. colleges in that State;
(c) if so, whether it is fact that NCTE is
sanctioning new D. Ed. colleges in large
numbers;
(d) whether Union Government have
conducted an enquiry into NCTE's D. Ed.
college sanctioning procedures; and
(e) whether Maharashtra Government
had requested to cancel the sanction of
eight D. Ed. colleges?
 Rural education cell
1535. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether concerned over the high
drop out rate of students in rural schools,
which have been facing neglect, besides
being deprived of basic amenities and
infrastructure, the National Council of
Educational Research and Training has
decided to constitute a rural education cell;
(b) if so, whether this cell would look

354
into the problems the schools are facing as
well as evaluate their performances; and
(c) if so, by when, a final decision in
this regard is likely to be taken?
 Utilization of unused budgetary
allocation for SSA
1536. SHRI C. RAMACHAN-
DRAIAH: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether, under the Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan Scheme (SSA), the schools are
permitted to utilise unused budgetary
allocation of the previous years during the
current year;
(b) if so, whether any case has come to
the notice of Government where, despite
the reservations expressed by a State
Project Director, the unused funds of SSA
have been channeled to award a
procurement contract to a tainted supplier;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
corrective actions taken thereon; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
 Foreign aid for Sarva Shiksha
Abhiyan
1537. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have been
receiving foreign aid during the current year
for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA);
(b) if so, the total amount of foreign aid
received for the SSA and the District
Primary Education Programme (DPEP)
during the last two years, programme-wise;
(c) whether the said amount is being
spent on SSA and DPEP; and
(d) the total amount of foreign
assistance spent, so far, on the said
programmes alongwith the balance amount
yet to be spent thereon?
 Promotion of students in classes VI to
VIII
1538. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Board of
Secondary Education (CBSE) has decided
not to mention pass or fail in the report
cards of the students studying in classes
VI to VIII;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) by when the A to E grading system
is likely to be introduced;
(d) whether the CBSE has also decided
not to detain any student even if he/she
scores an E grading; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
 English as stumbling block for
students
1539. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that, according to

355
the National Commission for Minority
Educational Institutions (NCMEI), English
remains a stumbling block for thousands of
students;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons therefor;
(d) whether Government are seriously
deliberating to prepare the students to
overcome this problem and to go ahead in
studies with brimming confidence; and
(e) if so, the steps taken/to be taken in
this direction?
 Brain drain in IITs
†1540. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that talented students educated
from the renowned IITs are generally
selected by foreign multinational companies
in the campus itself and taken abroad;
(b) the plan to make up the loss caused
to the nation with this kind of brain drain;
and
(c) the manner in which the financial
loss due to it would be made up?
 Central University in every State
†1541. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up a
Central University in every State of the
country;
(b) if so, whether any of the existing
Universities in the States would be given
the status of Central University or a new
university would be set up there;
(c) whether Uttarakhand has sent any
proposal for granting the status of Central
University to any university of the State;
(d) if so, the details thereof and whether
Government have received some more
proposals in this regard; and
(e) if so, the details of other proposals
received in this regard?
 Indian education in the international
market
1542. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to market the Indian education as a brand
in the booming international education
market;
(b) if so, the special features and
characteristics thereof;
(c) the steps taken in this direction and
the modes and technologies proposed to
be adopted for the purpose;
